extracted.intended_audience: readers and contributors of a scientific journal (Nature), including teachers, students, and technical practitioners evaluating books and preparing letters
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and informal standards used in Nature (book reviews and Letters to the Editor) for judging textbooks, technical handbooks, monographs and for handling submitted correspondence. Covers clarity, suitability for course level, completeness, illustrations, practicality of experiments, accuracy of standards, organization, and editorial submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and clarity of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment throughout is simple, which will render the book suitable for use in technical schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A textbook should present concepts plainly so it is appropriate for technical-school level; simplicity that nevertheless conveys correct methods is commended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of drawings and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings are well executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-executed illustrations help readability and comprehension; book judged favourably when drawings are clear and support the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability of the text
rubrics_metrics.description: The text is very readable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose style should be accessible to intended audience (students/teachers); readability is an explicit positive attribute in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and practicality of experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of many experiments which may be carried out on a comparatively small scale with inexpensive apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments that can be conducted with inexpensive, small-scale apparatus are particularly valuable for student instruction and increase the utility of a textbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical effectiveness through worked exercises and answers
rubrics_metrics.description: The book contains a number of well-selected exercises, with answers; to some of these exercises hints are appended for their solution, while others are left to the student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a mix of exercises with answers and hints to support learning while leaving some problems for independent work; selection quality matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness for intended audience / course level
rubrics_metrics.description: Will prove useful to engineering students in the first and second year of their course at a technical college.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the target course level; reviewers assess whether scope and depth match the needs of that level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters on the history, topography, population, political organisation, natural resources, industries, trade, transport, etc., with appendices of statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handbooks should cover essential topical areas relevant to the subject; inclusion of statistics and appendices adds value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of depth on fundamental aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: The notes on topography are very brief, covering scarcely two pages, while climate is dismissed in a few lines. More consideration of these fundamental aspects would enhance the value of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect sufficient treatment of fundamental topics (e.g., topography, climate); superficial treatment is a criticism and lowers the book's value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map quality and scale appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: A well‑printed, if rather small-scale coloured map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should be well printed and of appropriate scale for the topics discussed; too-small scale may limit usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency and correctness of terminology and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Engineering practice and phraseology change rapidly... examples: ‘mean spherical candle‑power’ is becoming obsolete; a ‘half‑watt’ lamp is now termed a ‘gas‑filled’ lamp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should use current terminology and reflect up-to-date engineering practice; obsolete phrases and outdated nomenclature are negative points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and completeness with respect to international standards
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not strictly correct to say that the international candle‑power 'is now defined as...' and the international standards for the resistance and temperature‑coefficients of pure annealed copper are not given, as they are of fundamental importance in electrical engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should correctly state definitions of units and include relevant international standards and fundamental constants where essential to the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate inclusion or omission of numerical tables
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope that the wire gauges, the table for the resistance of copper wires (temperature not stated), and the tables of fusing currents will be omitted from the next edition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical tables must include necessary context (e.g., temperature for resistance); otherwise they may be misleading and are better omitted or carefully qualified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and systematisation of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The pamphlet’s lack of system and reasonable completeness will somewhat diminish its value as compared with existing manuals of qualitative analysis such as that of Treadwell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange material systematically (preferably reflecting chemical relationships) and aim for reasonable completeness; ad hoc or fragmentary treatments reduce usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate organization reflecting subject relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: In arranging the elements according to alphabetical order, their chemical relationships are quite obscured, and the information conveys the impression of isolated snippets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize material to reflect natural/chemical relationships rather than arbitrary orders (e.g., avoid purely alphabetical ordering when it obscures pedagogy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and focus of coverage (distinctive contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinctive parts of the book are those that deal with the mode of fish‑curing and conservation, and with the utilisation of by‑products... Written with an evident personal knowledge of the processes described, these chapters make a really important contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight distinctive, well-informed sections where the author has personal/process knowledge; such contributions can significantly raise a book’s importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conciseness and balance between methods and results
rubrics_metrics.description: A well‑balanced account of oceanography, treated almost entirely from the physical point of view. The first part deals with methods... the second part deals with general results... The book is small but very concise in its treatment, and it is well illustrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An effective technical book balances methodological exposition and presentation of results, maintaining conciseness without sacrificing essential detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breadth of branch coverage vs depth (analytical methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deals briefly with all branches of the subject, and is illustrated. The section on analytical methods is brief, but most of the important determinations are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For comprehensive handbooks some breadth across branches is desirable, but critical analytical methods should be covered with adequate depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection bias and representativeness of examples/substances
rubrics_metrics.description: The selection of the inorganic and organic compounds is... quite arbitrary: one notices more particularly the substances studied by Dr. Fenton himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should strive for representative selection of examples; overemphasis on the author’s personal work can create a biased and less generally useful manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author expertise and personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Written with an evident personal knowledge of the processes described...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable personal practical experience or expertise in the subject matter enhances authority and the value of descriptive/process sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial submission policy for letters
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. Neither can he undertake to return, or to correspond with the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of NATURE. No notice is taken of anonymous communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents should not expect editorial endorsement of opinions; do not send anonymous communications; do not expect returned manuscripts or correspondence about rejected submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of simple, reproducible apparatus for public demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: A small experiment: a hand or a hand cut from white cardboard, feebly illuminated against a dark background, produces observable glows and after‑images; a small crystal of silver nitrate as a 'flat solid' with acidulated water renders a track visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For demonstrative notes or short communications, experiments that use minimal, inexpensive, and reproducible apparatus are valuable and suitable for publication as short notes or letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternative, non‑supernatural explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: Phenomena described by occultists (aura, luminous vapour) may be explained as retinal after‑images and eye movements rather than magnetic emanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting unusual observations, authors should consider and discuss plausible physiological or physical explanations and simple controls (e.g., cardboard controls, lighting conditions) before invoking extraordinary causes.
